evidence.note: Before building, the agent maps the surface: samples expected outputs per LSP method type (hover, documentSymbol, foldingRange, codeLens, selectionRange, callHierarchy) and spikes tree-sitter availability + parses individual Java files — de-risking the parser layer first.

Creates modules in explicit dependency order: main.rs/lsp.rs (protocol plumbing) → state.rs → analyze.rs (AST/symbol model) → handlers.rs (per-method) — a concrete layered hierarchy matching lexer→parser→AST→analysis→handlers.
Establishes done-checks per layer: builds, runs baseline run_tests, then writes diag.py as a per-method diagnostic — enabling method-by-method completion checks rather than one monolithic pass/fail.

Tackles methods one at a time (references, callHierarchy, documentSymbol, hover, typeDefinition, documentHighlight, semanticTokens), each diagnosed on specific files — later work builds on validated earlier layers.
'Categorize hover/references/highlight failures' — revisits the plan by grouping remaining failures per method to direct effort where value concentrates, a level-10 leaning behavior.
Repeated TodoWrite calls used to track milestone state across the long horizon (contents not visible in this condensed log).

reasoning: The agent breaks the enormous surface into an explicit module hierarchy (protocol → state → AST/symbol analysis → per-method handlers) written in dependency order, gets the handshake+parse working as a validated foundation, then iterates method-by-method with a dedicated per-method diagnostic and periodic failure-categorization to re-target effort — squarely the level-8 anchor. It shows glimmers of level-10 (early parser spikes, re-prioritizing by failure clusters), but I cannot confirm explicit leverage/risk sequencing or batching-by-shared-machinery from the condensed log (TodoWrite contents unreadable), so I hold at 8 with medium confidence.
